claims.text: Guangzhou Automobile Group Co., Ltd. is a Chinese vehicle maker headquartered in Guangzhou and controlled by the Guangzhou municipal government (Guangzhou SASAC).

source.name: GAC, GAC Global Site

claims.text: Moeve (formerly Cepsa) is owned by Mubadala Investment Company, Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, and The Carlyle Group.

source.name: Moeve, the company

claims.text: Riyadh Season is the flagship events season of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority, a government body.

source.name: Score and Change, Overview of the 2026/2027 La Liga sponsors

proposedRatings.reasoning: Saudi state events body (General Entertainment Authority); same Saudi state record that already rates Riyadh Air, Saudia and Visit Saudi as serious.
Majority-held by Mubadala, Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund; the UAE state money and mass-trial record put it at serious.
Municipal state-owned Chinese carmaker (Guangzhou SASAC). State money but no GAC-specific adverse finding located, so concern rather than serious, matching Gree.
Listed carmaker, but the State of Lower Saxony (~11.8%) and Qatar's sovereign fund (~17%) hold blocking stakes; minority state capital maps to concern.
Municipal government owner, not a sovereign state or fund; the same sub-national logic that rates the Diputacion de Malaga concern.
Malaga city tourism body owned by the city council; sub-national public owner, concern.
Provincial (Basque) government body on the Alaves front; sub-national public owner, concern.
Shenzhen-listed, family-controlled appliance maker; no state capital found.
Spanish retail bank, private/foundation owned, no state capital.
Low-cost brand of Vodafone Espana, part of the listed Vodafone Group.
London-listed rail ticketing platform, no state link.

unsourced: Score and Change (2026-27) says Abanca and Lowi each back two La Liga clubs but does not name the clubs: Abanca is placed on Celta Vigo and Deportivo La Coruna (both Galician) and Lowi on Getafe and Levante, inferred from the 2025-26 Blinkfire guide and geography; not confirmed by a 2026-27 source.
Osasuna (Digi), Real Betis (Trainline) and Villarreal (Ascale) back-of-shirt sponsors are taken from the 2025-26 Blinkfire guide and not re-confirmed for 2026-27.
Shorts sponsors are not fully mapped; the 2026-27 overview says 15 clubs have a back sponsor and six clubs carry multiple shorts brands, but only gives some names.
Espanyol, Elche, Rayo Vallecano, Valencia and Sevilla may have back-of-shirt or shorts sponsors not named in the sources used.
EBpay (Alaves sleeve), GCS (Rayo sleeve) and REVEL (Betis sleeve) ownership is opaque; recorded as private companies with no reliable primary source for the ultimate owner.
ODTY News and JP Financial are thin: both are brand names with little ownership information.
GAC's state ownership is well known but the fetched GAC site only confirms the company identity, not the Guangzhou SASAC control.
